thread.title: Weekend roundup: How to get your company lumped in with Sears | One good day for GE | How colleges help banks gouge students

author: Philip van Doorn
title: Weekend roundup: How to get your company lumped in with Sears | One good day for GE | How colleges help banks gouge students
text:
MarketWatch rounds up 10 of its most interesting topics over the past week.
1. Not a good look Cynical investors are used to verbal sleight of hand from corporate executives. After Kroger KR, +1.95% CEO Rodney McMullen talked up the food retailer’s digital sales efforts, an analyst couldn’t help but be reminded of similar talk years ago from Sears SHLDQ, +8.59% CEO Eddie Lampert. He also called Kroger’s stores “ rundown and dispiriting .” Sound familiar?
2. Analyst suggests GE is no longer a good short Shares of General Electric GE, -1.39% surged 7% on Dec. 13 — its biggest one-day gain in three years — after a JPMorgan analyst said the stock had fallen far enough .
3. Banks charge students high fees and pay colleges to enable the practice Banks that pay colleges to promote their services tend to charge students higher fees, according to a new report from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau .
Don’t miss: Feds arrest student debt-relief CEO who allegedly scammed borrowers out of $28 million
4. Technical warnings of the bull market’s end Here are six signs that the long bull market for U.S. stocks is coming to an end .
More on the stock market:
• Which Wall Street forecasters should you listen to now? Here’s who nailed it in 2018 (and who bombed)
• Finance Twitter: The 50 most important people for investors to follow
5. YOLO and losing a lot of money very quickly YOLO stands for “you only live once,” and that mantra can lead to some amazingly quick losses for traders .
6. A contrarian investment play with FAANG stocks The FAANG stocks — Facebook FB, -1.28% Amazon.com AMZN, -1.46% Apple AAPL, -2.08% Netflix NFLX, -0.19% and Google parent Alphabet GOOG, -0.34% GOOGL, -0.56% — have been among the bull market’s stars. But since the end of September, they have led the market lower with double-digit declines. Some investors believe it is now time to resume buying the FAANGs .
7. Then again, Apple may not overtake Microsoft Daniel Newman argues that Microsoft’s MSFT, -0.61% diversified software and hardware products give it a long-term advantage over Apple in the competition to be the largest U.S. company.
8. Cronos CEO has great expectations In an interview with Max Cherney, Cronos CRON, +1.67% CEO Mike Gorenstein says Altria’s MO, -1.67% huge investment can help turn marijuana into a standard consumer product .
9. What’s your (early) retirement number? We sum up the path to financial independence and retiring early in this one simple chart .
More on how to achieve financial independence: This is how your neighbors are preventing you from becoming a millionaire
10. The evil that people do Yes, some people really do give bad gifts on purpose .
